$comment: Inputs for pipeline:subbasins in reference mode (R3.5; owner decisions 2026-10-12). Hierarchy: level 0 = the region (id and name below), level 1 = the six APRHI basins exactly as the R3.1 roots in data/work/cba/basin/basins.geojson, level 2 = the 25 APRHI subcuencas, level 3 = the 80 APRHI unidades de gestión hídrica (UGH). Parents come from geometry, never from the source codes: a subcuenca's parent is the basin holding the largest share of its area, a UGH's parent the subcuenca holding the largest share; each child is clipped to its parent, and a parent's own area is the parent minus its children. The salar (Salinas Grandes) and the lagoon (Mar Chiquita) are not nodes: they stay in their basin's own area, as do the parts of whole basins outside the province. Layer paths are relative to data/raw/, read as the APRHI .prj files declare (EPSG:22174, always_xy; see gate.config.json). The UGH layer has one row without geometry (all attributes null); it is dropped and reported. Areas always come from the polygons (geodesic), never from the layers' area fields. Ids: regions/cba/subbasin-ids.json (created on the first run from rootSlugs and the source names, then fixed: the step fails when a feature has no id or an id has no feature). nameFixes are applied to every display name in order: 'exact' replaces a whole name, 'word' a word wherever it occurs. outletMinShare: a level-2/3 node has an outlet only if at least this share of its stream km drains to its largest-upland reach. reachMinShare: a reach goes to the subcuenca (then UGH) holding at least this share of its length, else it stays at the parent level. Level-1 outlets come from expectedExitReach in basin.config.json.
source: Portal de Información Hídrica de Córdoba (APRHI)

nameFixes.note: The Cuencas layer writes Carcaraña; IGN and the subcuenca and UGH layers write Carcarañá.
Missing accent in 'Rio Juramento Salado' (Cuencas layer) and wherever else a name starts with 'Rio '.
